evidence.attribution: Pádraig Harrington excerpt; creator explicitly credits Harrington footage to superspeedgolf
evidence.session: Earlier release feel and selected explanatory examples
evidence.summary: Harrington says that with the top of backswing in good order, the listener should feel hands firing/releasing immediately. He says the release will not literally happen that early but the feel is needed. He reassures the listener they are athletic enough not to cast. The premise and feel-versus-motion distinction must remain attached to the cue.

cases.observed_result: Rehearsals, manual guidance and practice montage; no controlled outcome. Creator explicitly reports ongoing course-transfer difficulty.
cases.title: Use an earlier-release feel when holding off release is the established problem
cases.coaching_finding: Creator criticizes holding angle/lag too long; Harrington excerpt presumes good top position and an athletic listener. No current student diagnosis is shown for this compilation.
cases.coach_reasoning: An exaggerated intention to release from the top may counter holding off; Harrington explicitly says the physical event will not happen exactly as early as the feel.

intervention.cue: Feel the hands release sooner from the top.
intervention.scope: Treat as a conditional sensation to test, not a command to throw clubhead past hands immediately.
intervention.source_claim_limits: No-cast, no-hook and impossible-too-early statements remain source assertions; they are not adopted as guarantees.

selection.policy_origin: User one-focus constraint. Eligibility and reassessment are proposed app rules, not a validated diagnostic test in this compilation.
selection.reassess: Check actual delivery and ball flight after the cue, then test on-course transfer; stop escalating the feel if strike or direction worsens.

limits: Self-report; no dates, comparative scores or measured retention.

source_ambiguities.issue: It needs to stop has an ambiguous biomechanical referent. Preserve verbatim meaning in raw transcript and visible manual comparison; no invented whole-body/arm stopping rule.
ASR repeats a previous wrist phrase in implausibly short segments over montage. Repetitions are not treated as independently supported narration.
Opening authority claim about combined major wins is promotional framing; titles/counts and identities of all four speakers are not verified.

cross_source_links.relation: Counterexample to a universal earlier-arms cue
cross_source_links.explanation: Menante’s TPI case has extreme lag but arms already early relative to trunk; the conventional casting explanation was rejected. This compilation cannot justify earlier hands from a lag appearance alone.

cross_source_links.relation: Release instruction must remain coordinated with body motion
cross_source_links.explanation: Cowen adjusts Danny’s motion when body outpaces arm and when calm becomes deceleration. These cases preserve matching/timing, while this compilation supplies a broad earlier-release feel.

cross_source_links.relation: Avoid turning explanation into handle dragging
cross_source_links.explanation: Danny’s excessive shaft-lean/handle-drag interpretation produced right-start issues. The ambiguous handle-forward language here should not become a universal maximize-lean cue.

cross_source_links.relation: Practice-to-course transfer remains a separate requirement
cross_source_links.explanation: Ruffels deliberately removes technical aids/thoughts for target work. McGrane’s post acknowledges that understanding and practising a feel for years has not guaranteed on-course transfer.

within_source_distinctions.relationship: Earlier-release feel is a conditional task; the force/stop passage is incomplete mechanism explanation. Do not stack an ambiguous stopping instruction onto the release cue.

annotation_opportunities: Show feel-versus-real qualification beside the earlier-release cue.
Keep each speaker/excerpt separately attributed; compilation agreement is not independent validation.
Pair manual guidance with original wording and mark undefined mechanical referents.
Record source self-reported transfer difficulty alongside practice footage.
excluded_material: Universal prohibition on holding angle in every context.
Guaranteed no-hook/no-cast result or verified speed gain.
Stopping the whole body or arms based on an ambiguous pronoun.
Promotional major-count claim as scientific evidence.

independent_validation.reason: Compilation with missing diagnoses, strong unsupported universals and ambiguous force explanation; useful conditional feel and transfer caveat retained.
